description: Typed current result families that an artifacts/** description asserts as registered while current-result-registry.json carries no result_kinds[] row for them. The gate tools/artifact_lint:asserted_result_families_are_registered refuses any such name that is not listed here, so this file is the visible ledger of assertions that outran the registry. It is a ratchet: entries may only be removed, and a listed family that becomes registered is itself an error.
adjudication: Opened 2026-09-19 with the gate. chris adjudicated on 2026-09-19 that artifacts/** descriptions are a normative surface, which is what makes an assertion here a registration claim rather than commentary. Seven names were asserted and none was registered. did_core_id was not a family at all -- the sentence meant that organization_id is a did_core_id -- and was rewritten to name the family it actually intends. mimi_room_binding and moderation_franking_proof were registered in the same batch because their subject and their value were both fully determined by the payload schema. The four below are not deletable and not mechanically derivable: each needs one design decision that the descriptions do not contain, so each is listed with the exact missing decision rather than guessed at. Do not add an entry to defer work that is derivable.

unregistered_families.reason: ak.moderation.decision asserts a keyed-set add onto subject target_ref with the fold hard_deny > quarantine > require_review. The element value is not derivable from moderation_decision_payload: the payload carries decision, action, reason_code, reason, effective_at and expires_at, and the description does not say which of those are part of the dot and which are audit provenance, nor what the dot key is. Registering it with the whole payload as the element would make expires_at part of set identity, which would fork one decision into two elements on any re-issue. Needs the dot shape decided in governance/content-moderation.md first.

Asserted by two writers with different closed payloads: ak.message.redact (message_id, track_name, preserve, mimi_provenance) and ak.redaction (target_ref, preserve), which the description says deliberately excludes Message. A shared family needs one subject spelling that both can produce -- message_id is not target_ref and target_ref MUST NOT spell ak:message: -- and one value shape that is not the union of two payloads. Needs models/event-and-patch.md to state the shared subject first.

ak.policy.rule asserts subject rule_id and an append-only projection where each accepted Event appends one revision rather than replacing the previous one. There is no append projection kind: the registered vocabulary is set, transition, merge, apply_patch and the three keyed_set forms. Registering it requires either adding a projection kind or expressing append as a keyed_set_add with a stated dot key, which is a change to the projection vocabulary and not a registry edit.

ak.view.reconcile asserts subject view_id and value = the whole View definition. models/views.md section 3.2 gives a second registered projection over the same subject under the family name view, written by ak.view.create and ak.view.update, and that name is not registered either. Registering view_reconcile alone would put two families on one view_id whose writers disagree about which is current; registering one family needs models/views.md to say whether reconcile replaces the same family's value or is a separate one, which the description does not say. Decide the family count first, then register both in one batch.

ak.organization.discovery asserts subject organization_id and a closed state value, and its payload def is the sibling of organization_moderation_policy_state_payload, which asserts the same shape in words this gate cannot see. The two should be registered together so the Organization surface does not acquire one registered family and one unregistered one, and that pairing needs the Organization state surface settled in governance/content-moderation.md rather than one row added here.
